_comment: Walk Reference — Realtime Database rules. v121 (13/08/2026).
Deny by default, then grant leaf by leaf. The boundary this enforces is the
one the whole system rests on: CLAUDE AUTHORS, THE APP ANNOTATES. Claude-
authored content — a task's text, urgency and provenance, a project's title
and summary, the plan, the take, the diffs, a note's resolution — is
READ-ONLY to the desk app and is only ever written by the server through the
admin SDK, which bypasses these rules. The desk may only touch the fields it
owns: what Richard did, who holds it, and what he wrote himself.
Adding a field to the desk app therefore means adding a line here, or the
write returns permission_denied. Note that a multi-path update() is checked
per child key: ref(action).update({done, status}) needs BOTH done and status
granted, or the whole update is refused.
The strategy record (v2, 13/08/2026) is the strict case of the same rule:
readable by Richard, writable by nobody. Its page does not write at all —
every observation, every piece of evidence and every scratch item is
authored by Claude through the server. There is no field for the app to own,
so there is no line here to grant.
The review store (v121, 13/08/2026) follows the strategy record exactly:
one uid may read, nobody may write, all writes go through the server's
admin SDK. Its window (review/index.html) only reads. This scoping is the
load-bearing security control for that document (review/SPEC.md §5) —
after deploying, verify it: signed out and signed in as any other account,
a read of /reviewStore must return permission_denied.
It is also the one node scoped by UID rather than by email claim, and the
difference matters. auth.token.email is only as trustworthy as the providers
enabled on the project: Google sign-in yields a verified address, but if
email/password or a custom-token provider is ever switched on, an attacker
can hold an UNVERIFIED email claim of any address and the rule passes. A uid
cannot be asserted — it is issued. The board's nodes still use the email form
and should be migrated the same way; they were left alone here only because
the desk app writes to a dozen of those paths and the change wants testing.
The uid is committed rather than left as a placeholder, deliberately. It is
not a credential — it is an opaque identifier Firebase issues, and nobody can
assert it without a token this project signed. A rules file that does not
match production is the greater hazard: this file calls itself the source of
record, so the next person to paste it verbatim would lock the account out.
Deploy: paste into console -> Realtime Database -> Rules -> Publish
(or firebase deploy --only database). This file is the source of record.
